items.title: API-Football and OddsAPI prices moving to a private store
items.what_was_wrong: API-Football's terms give no licence to publish its data, and the repos that hold raw price archives and prices inside our own ledgers are public.
items.what_changed: Every price-bearing file was inventoried and copied byte-exact to the private wowza-exec store. Nothing public was deleted and no live reader or writer changed yet; the cut-over is planned for Nov 22-24 behind a model parity gate, and the git history purge is deferred until after go-live. Owner 2026-11-17: the cut-over moves forward (dual-write from 17.11, zero-difference parity gate on 18.11, then the readers switch); it rolls back if anything differs.

items.title: Duplicate-fixture tie-break goes to the primary source
items.what_was_wrong: When two copies of the same match were equally complete, the loader kept whichever copy happened to sort last, so an unrelated data refresh could swap a football-data row for a backtest-archive row. This crashed a Pro Standard Repair run.
items.what_changed: Completeness still decides first; a tie now goes to the source ranked first (football-data, its cache, API-Football, then the backtest archive), and the date sort is stable.

items.title: Restored af_history rows verified and wired into the models
items.what_was_wrong: The provider rows recovered after the write-back data loss sat beside the history but no loader read them, so matches still had missing corners, fouls and cards.
items.what_changed: Each restored row was checked against API-Football; only rows whose full-time score matches are used, and a statistic is served only when API-Football holds the same value. The loader fills missing cells only and never overwrites an existing value (owner: "yes, make the models use them", "Exclude them").

items.title: af_history write-back data loss fixed; lost rows restored
items.what_was_wrong: A loader write-back replaced stored API-Football history rows with shots-only rows, wiping their full-time score, corners, fouls, cards and xG. Several collectors on data-truth-100 could drop columns they did not own in the same way.
items.what_changed: Writers now merge by key and change only the columns they own; they never drop a stored row or column. The lost rows were recovered from git history and stored beside the original file, which was not modified.

items.title: Props data audit: provider gaps read as missing, memory fix
items.what_was_wrong: Several props features read bad inputs: a drifting provider 'started' flag, unpublished provider counts read as 0, stale injury lists and raw shot counts whose definition changed. The props retrain also ran out of memory on the 16 GB runner.
items.what_changed: Started now comes from the collected lineups, unpublished counts stay missing, injuries are rebuilt from fixture lists and shots are league-relative. New checks 7d-7g catch a recurrence, and the harness memory fix keeps the frame identical. Props stay paper; nothing was promoted.

items.title: CLV capture bridges to the next kickoff (Nov 14 incident)

items.what_changed: A capture run now stays alive to reach a later kickoff it can still catch (run cap 170 -> 220 minutes). The incident is recorded as acknowledged; the health file still reports the unfiltered figure and the 40% floor is unchanged.

items.title: Empty lineup answers asked again
items.what_was_wrong: An empty lineups answer from right after full time was saved as final, so lineups the provider filled in later stayed missing for good.
items.what_changed: An empty answer is asked again at least 20 hours apart until kickoff date + 7 days, after new fixtures and inside the daily budget. Every answer is also kept in an append-only audit file.

items.title: Pro Standard Repair no longer crashes on a slice it cannot fit
items.what_was_wrong: The scheduled Pro Standard Repair run (43917999786) crashed in its forensic audit. One backtest-archive row (Antwerp v Beerschot VA, 2024-09-29) sat in a football-data season, which left a cross-validation fold with only one class. The row was there because of the v9 duplicate-fixture tie (fixed in PR #38).
items.what_changed: A slice that cannot be fitted (one class, too few minority rows or fewer than 100 rows) is skipped and reported with its reason; no class or AUC is invented. A missing AUC is no longer turned into 0.5: the verdict says NOT_TESTABLE. Integrity failures still fail the job.
numbers: 1 archive row in a football-data season caused the crash (Pro PR #3)
4 new tests; full Pro suite 420 passed, 0 failed (Pro PR #3)

items.title: Real data only: team/fantasy provenance (8a/8b/8c); v9_repaired retired
items.what_was_wrong: Live serving had drifted from training: provider season statistics overwrote six model features, home advantage used today's average, and duplicate fixtures got 0 rest days. The v9_repaired Standard model had learned xG and inside-box shots as 0.0 on every training row.
items.what_changed: Serving now uses training's derivation and refuses payloads with invented inputs; a fixture with no core form gets no probability. A provenance registry adds Data truth 8a/8b/8c, fantasy invented values were removed, and v9_repaired is retired (file kept for audit).

items.title: Score conflicts settled by goal events; awarded matches excluded
items.what_was_wrong: Football-data and API-Football disagreed on the score of 7 fixtures, and two history rows held a 3-0 forfeit instead of a played result.
items.what_changed: Each conflict was settled from API-Football's goal events and applied for every source. Awarded results are removed from the history, and rule 5 turns red on any served score that differs from the provider's 90-minute score without a settled decision.

items.title: COVID seasons left out of serving league averages
items.what_was_wrong: Training drops the COVID seasons, but live serving averaged league goals and away goals over the full history, so attack/defence strengths and home advantage differed from what the models learned.
items.what_changed: Serving league aggregates now exclude the COVID seasons, as every trainer does; team-level lookups keep the full history. The parity check was corrected, because it had the same skew on both sides and reported 0.

items.title: Data Truth 100 program and the stoplight gate
items.what_was_wrong: An A-to-Z audit found wrong names, invented defaults, missing data and misfiled leagues across the code and data, with nothing to stop them coming back.
items.what_changed: The audit findings were fixed and the owner's rules became RED/AMBER/GREEN checks. `python -m src.integrity.data_truth --gate` blocks a push when a gated rule is red or the known-defaults ceiling rises, and scheduled retrain/backtest workflows stay off until the milestone closes.
numbers: audit: 399 code sites in 5 repos, 7,702 data files profiled (729e25adc)
Data Truth register: 55 of 56 findings fixed with commits (fc1f9dc79)
known-defaults ceiling 39 -> 35 on main (038153bcb); 35 -> 0 on data-truth-100 (0704142d9)

rules.name: one canonical name
rules.checks: Every league value in boards, ledgers, player tips and history banks is a registry league.

rules.name: no silent defaults
rules.checks: No new invented default (literal fills, season fallbacks, 'or 0', price fills) in any production code.

rules.name: no missing data
rules.checks: The live board is priced and every served model track has all its inputs; banks are fresh.

rules.name: right league relations
rules.checks: No misfiled league rows in the banks, the registry validates, joins are league-keyed.

rules.name: one match, one row
rules.checks: No match stored twice and no provider fixture claimed by two served rows; served scores match the provider's 90-minute score.

rules.name: clean ledgers
rules.checks: From the Clean Record start: no multi or opposite tips, post-kickoff tips, invalid closes, duplicate player tips or twice-logged fixtures.

rules.name: props features
rules.checks: Keeper goals conceded match the score, team features read the right side, provider nulls stay missing (7d-7g drift checks on fix/props-data-audit).

rules.name: real data only
rules.checks: 8a active production violations, 8b new provenance violations (gated), 8c registered historical exceptions.

rules.name: no global bars in serving
rules.checks: No serving module reads a global or hand-set tier bar; tiers come only from each league's own approved bars.

rules.name: no retired tiers on future tips
rules.checks: No tip or stake record from the retirement date carries SNIPER / MARKSMAN / VALUABLE or a tier multiplier other than 1.

rules.name: bars rest on bet-time prices only
rules.checks: No approved bar rests on a price not proven captured before kickoff, and closing prices are never read as bet prices.

rules.name: injuries/lineups freshness
rules.checks: Collected injuries and lineups keep up with the matches played in each registry league.

items.rules_note: Rule numbers differ between branches until the go-live merge: on data-truth-100, 6 = clean ledgers, 7 = props features, 8a-8c = real data only; on prep/bars-oddsapi-hist, 6-8 are the bars rules, 9 = clean ledgers, 10 = props features. How 8 and 8a-8c are numbered after the merge is not recorded. main still runs rules 1-4, with 1, 2 and 4 gated.
